rows.what the ink shows: Above each Lambda there is a separate short raised n-shaped arch with a downward right end: one over the left Lambda and one over the right. On the left, the baseline u retains its rounded lower trough inside the closing parenthesis, and the raised star has distinct crossing arms; the equality strokes and right Lambda remain separable, but the terminal right u/star group merges with the cancellation.

A continuous heavy stroke covers the lower deleted baseline; isolated ascenders and a right-hand descender survive. The bodies of the proposed words cannot be separated reliably from that stroke and the distinct writing immediately above.

In the upper short cancelled line, upright strokes and a shallow bowl remain above the deletion, with two dark terminal uprights at the right. The connected baseline is concealed, preventing a secure reading of the whole proposed sequence.

The lower short cancelled line retains several downward strokes near its beginning and a taller isolated stroke farther right. The thick diagonal-horizontal deletion joins the intervening letter bodies and conceals the ending.

The raised phrase preserves a hooked initial stroke, a tall crossed stroke near its beginning, and paired tall strokes toward its end. The intervening rounded letters and the precise accent/cedilla detail are merged with the crossing lines, so the complete phrase remains uncertain.

A p-like descender projects below the long cancellation and a separate dot remains above the word; small terminal curves are also visible. The central letter bodies are flattened into the deletion stroke and do not establish the full spelling.
The small deletion beneath partir is a solid horizontal blot with one initial ascending stroke and a small peak near its right end. A separate d bowl and u trough cannot be distinguished.

A large summation zigzag and the right-hand parenthesized -1 with raised p survive. Dense diagonal cancellation crosses the lower bound, and the short upper fragment does not securely distinguish the superscript n.

The opening and closing parentheses and final dotted i with descending subscript p are visible. The leading symbol and first index/ellipsis group are crossed through by heavy diagonal and horizontal ink.

The inspected crop shows short horizontal ellipsis marks and one lowered comma-like stroke, without repeated angle signs. It does not independently expose both separator commas; their literal punctuation remains uncertain.

A small stem-and-shoulder subscript follows the final i, with short low strokes crowded against the following inequality. The ink does not let me account separately for n, a minus, and p, or securely reduce the group to p alone.

The cancelled character has a closed low bowl and short right-hand downstroke returning near the bowl base. There is no long descending right stem of q; the diagonal through its top is cancellation ink.
Immediately before the legible det, a dense dark blot and broad diagonal overstroke conceal the earlier character. No independent bowl-plus-ascender skeleton remains to establish d.

The left cancelled group has a hooked body and a detached mark at its upper right, compatible with si but too blotted for secure letters. A separate crossed De stands farther right and belongs to the next source mark, so it cannot resolve this left group.

A separate cancelled group after the left remnant has a tall D upright with a rounded right bowl, followed by a small open e loop. The D/e group is spatially distinct from the preceding remnant assigned to M1273.
A tall narrow l loop returns to the baseline, followed by a small low e turn and rightward exit. A horizontal cancellation runs across the lower strokes.

The cancelled group contains two surviving uprights and a broad descending diagonal, with the lower connecting strokes merged into the deletion. The inner loops needed to identify tout, or the two clean sides needed to isolate a Lambda, are not distinguishable.

Between exposant and alpha, a compact crossed group retains a leftward slant and a low enclosed-looking loop. The cancellation conceals the separate r, accented e and final l strokes, so réel remains uncertain.

After car, the heavy horizontal cancellation merges the small baseline strokes; a tall Lambda-like shape near x1220 has a separate short bar above it. The remaining strokes do not securely establish l’application or allocate that possible notation to a complete replacement.

The final cancelled run shows a tall initial h-like stroke, low humps, then a p-like descender and a tall curved terminal stroke. These suggest hermitien positif but the merged baseline prevents a secure full reading or verified word count.
